The study of coastal resilience and translating findings into practice is important for coastal communities, as well as the natural and economic systems that depend upon them.
As climate change impacts become more and more evident, disaster losses will continue to rise in the United States and across the world.

The next generation must face these challenges head on and the need to educate tomorrow’s decision makers about coastal resilience will only become more pressing.
Numerous national reports suggest that there is a critical need for multi- disciplinary research, teaching directed specifically at resilience-related issues, and an overall gap in translating resilience research into practice (1-3).

This program will build on 50+ years of success in the Department of Marine Affairs and draw on URI’s significant expertise in oceanography, ocean engineering, geology, and natural resources sciences.
Certificate programs in natural hazards and disasters are offered at other universities, although most are discipline-specific rather than multi-disciplinary.
Few have the demonstrated track record of URI in coastal and ocean research, nor have they focused on coastal regions and effectively addressed climate change in communities where the design of human settlements reflect past, rather than future, environmental conditions.

This certificate program will link between climate change adaptation and coastal resilience and draw on the expertise of URI faculty from the physical and social sciences to educate students about policy-relevant research that can be applied in the work force.
